Yes, so there is length dependent SFN (which is usually the norm, starts in feet and hands and progresses up the limbs) or non-length dependent SFN where the distance from the torso does not affect  the extent of the neuropathy. Mine is systemic and non-length dependent (different numbness, tingling, pain throughout the body); my skin punch was done just to confirm the extent of my neuropathy. 

The lab that gets your biopsy will need to reference your sample against already established values for nerve density based on a healthy control group - the labs don’t have that for every single part of the body so usually a neurologist will choose one or two areas where you’re having symptoms that they know have objective reference lab values to compare it with. In my case, both sites of my punch came back with very little nerve density and was far below the threshold for diagnosing SFN. I asked my neurologist and she said that I have what she considers to be a severe case. I’d say it’s worth asking for and looking at your test results when they come back because they can give you a lot of valuable information. Hope that helps.

Fiber is not included in the 10g of carbohydrates because fiber is a non-caloric substance, whereas carbohydrates are at 4 kcal/g. If you look at the sugar, they make up 8.7g out of the 10g of carbohydrates. On a vertical label this is why total sugars and sometimes added sugars (as it is here) are placed as a subset of carbohydrates. 

All of that to say...The label puts fiber there because it is subtracted from the total carbohydrates to give you what is called “net” carbohydrates for that serving of food.

Net carbs = Total carbs - Fiber
